title: The highway that wouldn’t
stop running.
caption: A sandstone spire holds the last of the day. The road that brought me here was named, in the end, by a man who simply would not stop running — and I understood him better than I expected to.

title: Below the sea,
above the sky.
caption: This place earned its name. Below sea level, above the clouds, nothing in between except the heat and a few honest thoughts about endings.

title: Please never
find me.
caption: I’m going to hide somewhere in Arizona. There are folds in the red rock big enough to lose a life inside of, and most days that sounds like an offer worth considering.

title: The biggest
of all.
caption: No photograph survives this place. You stand at the rim and the scale rearranges your idea of what a hole in the earth can be.

title: Is this
even real.
caption: The walls move like fabric. The light arrives once a day and the rest is patience. Solo‑traveller souls share looks and ask nothing.

title: Twenty‑nine, beside
two thousand.
caption: Twenty-nine years doesn’t feel like a lot when you’re standing next to ladies who were here for two thousand. The forest does not console you so much as quietly correct your sense of proportion.

title: On the way to
Angels Landing.
caption: Nature never disappoints, at least not in Utah. The trail folds itself into the cliff like a question being asked over and over, and the answer is — keep climbing.

title: Could not
sleep.
caption: 4:30 AM, could not sleep. 5:21 AM, no sun today. 5:25 AM, sun left the chat. A short obituary for a morning that almost happened.

title: A random
blessing.
caption: A random blessing on the way out of the woods. Love ya, golden hour. We’ll meet again, probably when I’ve given up on you.

title: Memorial Day,
Mist Trail.
caption: The Memorial Day crowd got me. The bears did not. Halfway up I forgot what I was here for and let the spray decide.

title: My favorite
energy.
caption: Welcome to Lommelwood. Two-stroke, four-stroke, sunburn, beer, the kind of cheering you feel through your shoes. A reminder that beauty doesn’t have to be quiet to be holy.

title: Pacific Park,
no one awake.
caption: Early morning, no crowd. Fresh air and a rising sun at one of the most iconic spots in the world. Briefly, the carousel was mine.

title: Away from
the crowd.
caption: A road folds itself into the hills until the city is just a hum behind you. Two small figures, one long bend, the rest is quiet.

title: Restless ocean,
endless peace.
caption: Black sand, white waves, one figure that did not bring a watch. The Pacific keeps its own time and lets you in for free.

title: Precious moments
from San Francisco.
caption: The bridge, the bay, the fog still figuring out how to be a city. A few hours that I keep getting back to in my head.

title: Beauty of
the woods.
caption: A polaroid pinned to a forest. The trees pretended not to notice, and the photograph stayed anyway.

title: Woke up an
excited kid.
caption: First real snow of the year and the woods agreed to play. The kid that lives somewhere in the back of all of us showed up uninvited.

title: Last
May.
caption: The sandstone keeps a record of light that doesn’t need a calendar to read it back. A return trip in the head, half a year later.

title: Edge of
everything.
caption: One small figure on a long ledge. The canyon does what it always does — it stays, and it makes the rest of us look briefly honest.

title: Walking back
through it.
caption: Two people, one trail, two-thousand-year-old neighbors. The path remembers more than we ever will.

title: One evening
in February.
caption: A red lighthouse, blue hour, dune grass that pretends to listen. The kind of evening you write down so you don’t lose it.

title: Art and
ghost town.
caption: The walls keep painting themselves. The people left a long time ago. I stayed for an afternoon and the wall waved back.
